decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core heat-exchange range in a growing market, it likely has low incremental carrying cost and after only one year its commercial value is still too uncertain to justify abandonment.

This condenser fits the firm's established engineering base and customer set, so real-options logic favors keeping it on the market until more market feedback arrives rather than closing the option early.

Even if similar to other condenser offerings, it is close to the existing portfolio and inexpensive to maintain relative to potential project wins, so management would likely wait for clearer evidence before dropping it.
The tube-liner product builds directly on the firm's service and repair capabilities, where add-on offerings usually cost little to keep available and can create valuable aftermarket opportunities.
A customized industrial air cooler is highly aligned with the firm's solutions business and likely needs more than one year to reveal its order potential, so keeping the option open is sensible.
Repair inserts support the installed base and service model, making them a low-risk adjacent offering whose upside can still unfold with limited ongoing commitment.
